messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike in 5xx + timeouts for /v1/generate across gateway (us-east-1). 5xx rate up to 12% over last 5m, tail latency >3s. Sample log snippet shows "upstream response returned error" from model-proxy but no request_id present. Pager: carla-oncall
carla-oncall: acked. I'm on it — grabbing logs and checking dashboards. tagging @alice-sre and @bob-runtime. :eyes:
alice-sre: I'm looking at ingress/gateway logs now. We're seeing a high number of upstream 502/504 from model-proxy nodes. Traces for those requests are sparse — sampling looks low for the gateway route. Also noticed request-id header is absent in a lot of the gateway->proxy calls.
bob-runtime: adding context — we did a rolling deploy to model-proxy yesterday (rev: gp-2026-03-12-8f2). Could be related. I can pause new rollouts if needed.
dave-support: several customers reported timeouts in us-east-1, most on dedicated pools. Escalation coming from accounts: acme-inc, fastsuit. They see "gateway timeout" in client logs.
carla-oncall: quick plan: 1) add stopgap instrumentation to get request_id propagation + higher tracing for the affected path 2) a routing fallback to a smaller model variant for critical customers 3) scale up model-runner pool if deploy rollback not immediate. Who can make the prototyping changes? alice?
alice-sre: I'll push temporary logging to gateway and bump trace sampling for /v1/generate to 100% for the next 15m. Also will add header propagation in envoy filter to ensure X-Request-Id is set and forwarded. Paste of command I'll run:

```
# bump gateway trace sampling (temporary)
curl -X POST https://internal-config.redwood/tracing/sampling \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","sample_rate":1.0}'

# patch envoy to always set X-Request-Id if missing
kubectl -n gateway patch configmap envoy-filters --patch '{"data":{"set_request_id":"true"}}'
``` 

I will also create a short-lived prom metric for in-flight requests on model-proxy and push sample events to our pushgateway so we can visualize the backlog.
bob-runtime: I'll prepare a feature-flagged fallback route to small-model-v1 and enable it for a subset of traffic from us-east-1 (critical customers only). using redwoodctl:

```
redwoodctl feature set fallback_to_small_model --on --scope region:us-east-1 --owners bob-runtime,carla-oncall --ttl 30m
```

and a temporary routing rule:

```
# route critical customer ids to fallback
redwoodctl route add --from /v1/generate --to small-model-v1 --if "user in [\"acme-inc\", \"fastsuit\"]" --priority 50
```

dave-support: can we also enable synthetic pings for the dedicated pools so we can measure success for customer tickets?
eva-product: adding note for customer comms — will draft an interim message once we have mitigation status.
carla-oncall: I'm seeing that model-runner pods in us-east-1 are at CPU saturation and connection queues rising. I'm going to increase runner replicas by +50% for now and set a higher concurrency limit.

```
kubectl -n model-runner scale deployment model-runner --replicas=12
# increase concurrency env for pod template
kubectl -n model-runner set env deployment/model-runner MAX_CONCURRENCY=24
```

alice-sre: deployed the envoy patch and trace sampling is up. I'm seeing request_ids now in logs and traces are connecting gateway->proxy->runner. Creating a temporary Prom push for `model_proxy_inflight` so dashboards show the backlog:

```
echo "model_proxy_inflight 12" | curl --data-binary @- http://pushgateway.internal:9091/metrics/job/model-proxy/instance/us-east-1
```

also increased jaeger sample rate; traces coming through. Correlating a few traced failed requests — most fail with a 504 from runner and a long queue wait.
bob-runtime: fallback route enabled for acme-inc + fastsuit. Confirming requests are hitting small-model-v1 for a subset. Early telemetry shows lower error rates for those IDs.
dave-support: notified acme-inc that we're investigating and have a partial fallback. They're asking for ETA.
carla-oncall: mitigation checklist update:
- [x] enable request-id / logs: done
- [x] increase trace sampling: done
- [x] temporary in-flight metric: done
- [x] fallback routing for critical customers: done
- [x] scale model-runner replicas: done
- [ ] determine root cause (deploy vs saturation)

alice-sre: initial hypothesis: rollout to model-proxy introduced a regression in the proxy's connection handling (fd leak / slower upstream drains) that caused queueing downstream. Because we lacked propagated request_id and sampling, the problem surface was fuzzy. Once we had traces the correlation is clearer.
bob-runtime: I can roll back the model-proxy deploy (gp-2026-03-12-8f2) if we decide. Rolling back will cause short reconnection churn but should remove the regression.
carla-oncall: let's roll back to gp-2026-03-10 stable for model-proxy, but only after we've confirmed fallback coverage and increased capacity. Alice — can you coordinate the rollback? We want to avoid additional customer impact.
alice-sre: rolling back now. Command:

```
redwoodctl deploy rollback model-proxy --to-revision gp-2026-03-10-stable --region us-east-1
```

Monitoring... logs show reduced 5xx after terminating the problematic pods. Error rate dropping from 12% -> 3% over 6 minutes. latency tail improving.
carla-oncall: great. keep rollback running and we'll monitor for 15m then start handoff. dave, can you own comms to the big affected customers?
dave-support: yes — sending messages now. will follow up in #customer-updates with copy.
eva-product: drafting a public status update (we'll coordinate wording with legal). Outline: degraded service in us-east-1 impacting generation for some customers, fallback and scaling applied, rollback in progress, investigations ongoing.
carla-oncall: note on observability gaps: root cause summary will include lack of propagated request_id, low trace sampling, and missing in-flight metric limits. Action items post-incident:
- add integration test that validates X-Request-Id propagation across gateway->proxy->runner
- make trace sampling for customer-critical routes default to 10% (and allow quick bump to 100% via runbook)
- instrument model-proxy to export in-flight queue length and fd usage to prometheus
- run a chaos test for model-proxy connection handling

alice-sre: filing follow-up tickets now and adding runbook tasks. I'll create a temporary dashboard that persists and add alert thresholds for model_proxy_inflight > 10.

```
# follow-up ticket titles
- INFRA-1227: ensure X-Request-Id propagation in gateway & proxy
- INFRA-1228: model-proxy in-flight and fd metrics
- INFRA-1229: runbook: bump tracing & fallback routing steps
```

carla-oncall: handing off to @bob-runtime for next oncall window. summary: rollback completed, error rate down to ~1.8% baseline, small-model fallback still enabled for critical customers (ttl left ~18m). Observability added for now; permanent fixes in tickets above. passing to bob — please take a look and keep an eye for regression.
bob-runtime: taking handoff. I'll keep fallback on for 30m then disable unless we see regression. I'll also run a quick canary deploy for a patched model-proxy build that includes fd fix.

ops-bot: Handoff recorded. New oncall: bob-runtime. Incident severity: SEV3 -> moving to monitoring. Incident duration so far: ~48 minutes.

carla-oncall: final note — thanks all. postmortem scheduled for tomorrow 11:00 with SRE + runtime + product. capture notes in #postmortems after the meeting. :white_check_mark:

-- end of thread --
